Asha — thanks for the sample. Quick summary from our simulator and ops assessment (attached workbook: redwood_model_matrix_v1.xlsx). I ran it against three candidate variants tuned for your workload. Notes below are focused on the patient-facing summarization path (avg input 120 tokens, avg output 80 tokens).

Model shortlist (recommended):
- M1-medium-32Q (quantized 32-bit profile) — best cost balance. P50: 180ms, P95: 420ms (single-request), tokens/sec ~120. Good for baseline.
- M2-low-latency-8Q (low-latency optimized, more memory) — P50: 90ms, P95: 260ms, tokens/sec ~240. Higher cost (~1.8x) but meets aggressive P95 targets.
- M3-high-context (long-context 64k) — P50: 240ms, P95: 520ms for long-window requests (not necessary for summaries, reserve for triage where clinical context spanning several messages matters).

Hourly token map (derived from sample CSV):
- Baseline average hourly tokens (in+out): 2.1M tokens/hr across the entire integration during business hours.
- Peak 9–10am: 3.8M tokens/hr. Peak 19:30–20:30: 3.2M tokens/hr.
- 70% of requests are <256 token context; 18% are 256–2k (triage threads), 12% are >2k (rare longitudinal threads).

Ops recommendations (concise):
1) Route summary flows to M2-low-latency-8Q with 16-request batching during peaks. That preserves P95 < 300ms with batching latency budget set to 25ms on the client side.
2) Use prefix KV caching for patient stable context (patient profile + recent messages) — expect 18–25% token savings on repeat interactions.
3) Reserve M3-high-context for triage/offline batch jobs; use canary routing for 2 weeks before full switch.
4) Set autoscale thresholds for Dedicated pool: scale up at sustained >2.5M tokens/hr for 10 consecutive minutes.

Attachments: redwood_model_matrix_v1.xlsx (sheets: latency_by_seq, cost_estimates, hourly_token_map).

Open questions for Friday:
- Confirm target P95 for summaries (Tessa flagged 500ms? Is 300ms the target?)
- Any regulatory requirement for on-prem model variants or private deployment for triage data?

I'll present these slides and the workbook on Friday.

—Monica
